heroHeadline: Post-Summit Bifurcation Structural: Zero H200 Chips to China, Huawei Ascend at 750K Units — MIIT Deepens Manufacturing-AI Integration as Rare Earth Leverage Holds
heroSubtitle: One week after the Trump-Xi Beijing summit (May 14–15, 2026), the US-China tech war has consolidated into a clear bifurcation that no diplomatic exchange reversed. Zero Nvidia H200 chips have shipped to China despite US Commerce Department approval for approximately 10 firms (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, JD.com, Lenovo): Beijing directed firms to pause orders, and the licensing framework reportedly requires Nvidia to remit 15–25% of China sales revenue to the US government — a commercial condition China is using to justify routing procurement entirely to domestic Huawei Ascend chips. Rare earth exports remain ~50% below pre-restriction levels, with Beijing continuing to wield mineral leverage post-summit. On the domestic chip side: Huawei Ascend 950PR planned shipments for 2026 total ~750,000 units, with ByteDance's $5.6B order (~350K units) covering roughly 50% of annual supply; Huawei commands ~60% of China's domestic AI chip market and projects $12B in AI chip revenue (+60%+ YoY). MIIT Minister Li Lecheng (Bloomberg, May 16) reaffirmed the manufacturing-AI integration strategy that serves as the demand-side flywheel for China's domestic chip ecosystem: AI into manufacturing → domestic AI chip demand → fab capex (SMIC Q1 $2.51B, Q2 +14–16%; Hua Hong $6B Wuxi bet) → reduced strategic dependence on US hardware. China's generative AI user base hit 600 million (Bloomberg/CGTN, May 12) — up 142% year-over-year — while ByteDance Doubao alone processes 120 trillion tokens daily. The US-China AI safety dialogue channel announced May 14 is the only institutionalized summit output. The post-summit verdict: symbolic stabilization achieved; structural technology bifurcation accelerating.
